title: Surface a refused agent relocation variable in entire status

verdict.rationale: The evidence covers the original writing of these functions (transcript-path ownership matching, Codex trust checks) but never mentions how a refused relocation variable should be handled or surfaced. The DEBUG-only logging on fail-open is not something the recorded evidence shows was chosen; it is a gap the issue describes as a follow-up.

evidence.text:
Fix Cursor session mis-identified as Claude Code

When Cursor IDE forwards a single user prompt to both .cursor/hooks.json
and .claude/settings.json, two `entire` hook processes race to claim the
session and the loser's wrong agent_type can win the last write.

Three layered defenses:
- SessionStart hint: first agent to fire claims the session ID
  (`<sessionID>.agent` written with O_EXCL).
- Transcript-path override: a transcript inside an agent's session dir
  is authoritative — overrides both hint and the firing hook.
- Per-session file lock: serializes concurrent InitializeSession calls
  so the runner-up takes the cheap update path (`correctSessionAgentType`)
  instead of also creating-from-scratch. Lock files live under
  `<git-common-dir>/entire-locks/` to keep `entire-sessions/` clean.

Surface untrusted Codex hooks in the SessionStart welcome

When entire ships a new hook (the recent PostToolUse addition is the
first instance, more will follow), users who trusted earlier versions
of our hooks won't have a \`trusted_hash\` entry for the new one in
their ~/.codex/config.toml. Codex's own startup warning catches this,
but it's generic — the user has to read the /hooks UI to figure out
which hook came from where.

Reaching the SessionStart hook handler proves SessionStart is itself
trusted, so it's the right place to add a contextual nudge: if any
other event we declared in .codex/hooks.json lacks a state entry under
the same hooks-file path, append a one-liner naming the missing events
to the welcome message.

Detection is structural — we read the user's config.toml and look for
\`[hooks.state."<hooks.json>:<event>:<group>:<handler>"]\` headers, no
hash recomputation. That misses the "command changed, hash mismatched"
case (status = Modified), but Codex's own warning still surfaces it,
so we don't need to. The check stays cheap and free of the brittle
hash-replication coupling we declined for production pre-trust.

Codex-only: other agents don't have a per-user trust gate.
